comments.author: rlalik
comments.body:
Hi, original issue reporter here.

Upon request of @mbyrnepr2  in https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/issues/9727 I tested the PR-version and it works fine for my case for both `tox.ini` and `setup.cfg` with proper config files autodetection.

comments.author: github-actions[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 According to the primer, this change has **no effect** on the checked open source code. 🤖🎉

*This comment was generated for commit e0a456d5e35ac3c0c67bf429c4448886d1307873*

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body: Why make this a constant? Can't it be like `setup.cfg`?

review_comments.author: mbyrnepr2
review_comments.body:
Thanks @DanielNoord. Agreed.
While I have your attention, what's your opinion on [this logic](https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/blob/main/pylint/config/find_default_config_files.py#L64) and the associated comments around the inconsistencies mentioned on the issue? It does feel like we should allow `[pylint]` and not necessarily `[pylint.something]` but there could be some rationale for that.

Our own [documentation](https://pylint.pycqa.org/en/latest/user_guide/usage/run.html#command-line-options) has this: _setup.cfg in the current working directory, providing it has at least one pylint. section_

review_comments.author: Pierre-Sassoulas
review_comments.body:
```suggestion
    for file_name in ("fake.cfg", "tox.ini"):
        fake_conf = tmp_path / file_name 
        with open(fake_conf, "w", encoding="utf8") as f:
            f.write(content)
        assert _cfg_has_config(fake_conf) == expected
```

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body:
Yes, we previously only allowed `pylint.` because the way `optparse` worked required sections. I removed that when migrating to `argparse` and improving support for `toml`.

I would support changing this to be 1. exactly "pylint" or 2. anything that starts with "pylint.". To make sure we are not starting to parse `"pylint-internal-plugin"` etc.

review_comments.author: mbyrnepr2
review_comments.body: FYI @Pierre-Sassoulas and also may need to wait/further refactor before merging.

review_comments.author: Pierre-Sassoulas
review_comments.body: Thanks for the ping :) I think anything starting with ``pylint.`` is closer to what's happening in pyproject.toml so I would favor that.

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body: In `.toml` we support `[tool.pylint]`. I think making `.ini` in line with this makes sense.

review_comments.author: Pierre-Sassoulas
review_comments.body:
Should we make the ``tool`` mandatory ? As in ``[tool.pylint]``, or ``[tool.pylint.main]``, ``[tool.pylint.basic]`` (etc.). We don't in ini file currently, but the ini file is pylint specific so it doesn't need the "pylint" / "tool.pylint" part.

https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/blob/2ba88b9317ff37a1e94007d00bbcad65ed515e18/examples/pylintrc#L119

So maybe  ``[pylint]``, or ``[pylint.main]``, ``[pylint.basic]``. for consistency in tox.ini (consistency with file of the same format above consistency with toml), and backward compatibility in ini ?

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body:
`tool` is a thing because of the `pyproject.toml` spec I think.

Seeing other `tox.ini` files I think nobody would be surprised that `[pylint]` would be parsed as the configuration for `pylint`. We currently require people to do`[pylint.some_section_that_isnt_even_validated]` which feels cumbersome and inconsistent. That's why I proposed changing it from only `[pylint\..+]` to also allow `[pylint]`.

review_comments.author: mbyrnepr2
review_comments.body: Ok thanks folks! I've  tried to match Daniel's vision with the latest commit; accept `[pylint]` or `[pylint.<something_arbitrary>]`. Let me know if I've gotten anything wrong!

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body: We should probably include the change about accepted sections here as well.

+++ b/doc/whatsnew/fragments/9727.bugfix
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+Fix a bug where a ``tox.ini`` file with pylint configuration was ignored and it exists in the current directory.
+
+``.cfg`` and ``.ini`` files containing a ``Pylint`` configuration may now use a section named ``[pylint]``. This enhancement impacts the scenario where these file types are used as defaults when they are present and have not been explicitly referred to, using the ``--rcfile`` option.
+
+Closes #9727
